_calibration: gated: fetched from the reference dataset and merged by fetch_reference.py

files: consensus_fa.nii.gz (voxelwise median FA of the panel)
consensus_md.nii.gz (voxelwise median MD of the panel)
roi_mask.nii.gz (b0 brain mask eroded by two voxels)

weight_basis.fa_agreement: FA is the graded file of the output contract, and its pattern is what every defensible fit shares: choices of shells and estimator move its level, not where the white matter is.
weight_basis.fa_level: A little weight on level as well, so a map with the right pattern on the wrong scale does not pass as if it were right; the full-credit line is generous because the shells used move FA by a few hundredths.
weight_basis.md_agreement: MD is asked for and graded, by pattern only: its level depends on the shells used (the panel's medians differ by half), and r reads every unit the same.

zero_line_basis: FIXED, not calibrated: where a map earns nothing. Measured against these zero lines (analysis_06_fit_panel.sh in the build), the other control's FA reaches r 0.33 and a left-right mirrored FA 0.39, against r 0.91 or more between any two panel fits; the other control's MD reaches r 0.31 against 0.71 or more within the panel; noise sits at 0.
slack_basis: The full-credit lines are the panel's own leave-one-out spread -- the lowest r and the largest median difference of a member against the median of the others -- widened by these, since a seventh defensible fit may land a little outside six.
threshold_basis: within_reference_variability means every metric at full credit. The pass line is the benchmark-wide 60: FA in agreement and level with no MD scores 70 and passes, an FA map of the wrong brain scores under 10.

gate_basis.fa_present: FA is the graded file; without it there is nothing to score.
gate_basis.geometry_matches: Maps are compared voxel by voxel on the acquisition's grid; a map resampled elsewhere is not the native-space map the task asks for.
gate_basis.fa_in_range: FA is bounded by 0 and 1 by definition. Fits write it a little above 1 where an eigenvalue comes out negative: at most 0.34 % of brain voxels in any panel fit, so up to 1 % passes, and a map on another scale, with most voxels out of range, does not. A constant map inside the brain -- all zeros, as a fit on an unusable gradient table writes -- carries no fit.
